executive_summary: This page is a face-value ticket listing dressed up as a deal — all four ticket tiers show identical original_price and deal_price (no discount), yet the page still flags 'limited time' urgency, which is misleading and a refund/dispute risk. The biggest conversion levers are not price cuts but (1) fixing the empty highlights and fine_print sections, which currently just echo section headers ('Need To Know Info', 'Where To Redeem'), (2) reframing value against Universal Hollywood ($109+) and Paramount ($69+) so $79 reads as the mid-priced, guide-led, behind-the-scenes option, and (3) preempting the two dominant negative review themes — perceived value and 'moving like cattle' pacing — by surfacing what's actually included (3-hour total experience, 1-hour expert guide, real working backlot). Age restriction (5+, with 5–17 requiring an adult) is completely missing from the page and is a known purchase blocker for families.
competitive_positioning: Against direct alternatives, $79 for the WB Studio Tour sits between Paramount's $69 walking tour and Universal Studios Hollywood's $109+ theme-park admission — and unlike Universal, WB is a real working backlot with a guided experience. The page should explicitly own the 'authentic working studio, expert-guided, 100+ years of film history' lane rather than competing on price. Booking direct on wbstudiotour.com is the same price, so Groupon's edge here is discoverability, bundling with nearby LA deals, and the 4.79★ social proof from 441+ Groupon buyers — none of which the current page leverages. Because there is no actual discount, every recommendation below assumes the job is to convert undecided shoppers comparing LA studio tours, not to sell on savings.

recommendations.proposed_value:
• 1-hour guided tour led by an expert WB Studio Tour Guide, plus 2 hours self-guided exploration (3 hours total)
• Walk real working backlots where 100+ years of films and TV shows have been made
• Step inside iconic indoor stage rooms — repeatedly called out by reviewers as the highlight
• Available in English, Spanish, or French — pick your language at checkout
• Upgrade option: TCM Classic Films Tour adds the Property Department, Rose Garden, and golden-age film clips (3.5 hours total)
• 4.79★ from 441+ Groupon buyers; 810+ already booked
recommendations.rationale: The current 'highlights' are literally section header labels, not benefits. The description buried in prose contains all the actual selling points (duration, languages, TCM extras) and Yelp reviewers single out 'Inside of a Stage Room' and the guides as the best parts — none of which surface above the fold.
recommendations.evidence: Audit: highlights = ['Need To Know Info', 'Where To Redeem']; description mentions '3 hours total (1-hour tour with guide + 2 hours self-guided)'. Yelp: 'Inside of a Stage Room' called out as a highlight; 'tour guide was friendly, knowledgeable, and genuinely entertaining.'
recommendations.expected_impact: Largest single conversion lever — moves the page from a ticket-listing layout to a benefit-led deal page and gives undecided shoppers reasons to click buy.

recommendations.proposed_value:
• Valid for tour date selected at checkout; reservations required
• Ages 5+ only — children under 5 are not permitted on any tour
• Guests ages 5–17 must be accompanied by an adult 18 or older
• Plan for ~3 hours on site (TCM tour: ~3.5 hours), including post-tour Stage 48 exhibit, gift shop, and dining
• Tour operates rain or shine; comfortable walking shoes recommended
• Wheelchair-accessible carts available free of charge — request at booking
• Photo ID required at check-in; arrive 30 minutes before tour time
• Not valid with other offers; see merchant site for full terms
recommendations.rationale: Empty fine print on a $68–$99 timed-entry ticket is a refund magnet. The 'ages 5+ / under-18 needs an adult' rule is hard policy from wbstudiotour.com and a documented purchase blocker for families. Accessibility info is also a real shopper question per the search results.
recommendations.evidence: Audit: fine_print = ''. wbstudiotour.com Terms: 'Children (under 5 years of age) are not permitted on the Tour. All minors, ages 5 – 17, must be accompanied by a person aged 18 years or over.' wbstudiotour.com Special Assistance: 'Our carts support most wheelchair types... We loan wheelchairs free of charge.'
recommendations.expected_impact: Reduces post-purchase refund/dispute volume and removes the #1 family-buyer hesitation (can my kid go?).

recommendations.proposed_value: Remove the 'limited time' badge. Replace with a truthful scarcity cue tied to inventory: 'Tour times sell out — book at least 3 days ahead' or '810+ booked on Groupon' (already true).
recommendations.rationale: All four ticket tiers have original_price == deal_price (no discount). Calling this 'limited time' on a face-value ticket is misleading and erodes trust if a shopper price-checks against wbstudiotour.com. The 810+ bought label is real social proof and a more honest urgency substitute.
recommendations.evidence: Audit: prices show $79=$79, $78=$78, $68=$68, $99=$99 with discount_pct=null on all four; bought_label = '810+ bought'.
recommendations.expected_impact: Protects brand trust and avoids regulatory/PR risk on deceptive urgency; honest scarcity still drives booking.

Does Groupon have any negotiated upside here (early access, behind-the-scenes extra, bundling with another LA deal) that would let the page offer more than face-value parity with wbstudiotour.com?

Why is the French-language tour priced $11 lower than English ($68 vs. $79)? If this is a legitimate ongoing differential, lead with 'From $68'; if it's a data error, fix before the title/meta changes go live.
